ing: 2 lb boneless skinless chicken breast, bite-sized
1 can (10 oz) mild red enchilada sauce
1 can black beans, drained and rinsed
1 small can mild diced green chiles
2 tsp chili powder · 1½ tsp cumin · 1 tsp garlic powder · 1 tsp onion powder · 1 tsp smoked paprika · ½ tsp oregano
st: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Put the chicken, uncooked rice, onion, bell pepper, corn, black beans, green chiles and garlic straight into a 9×13 dish.
Season with the spice blend plus salt and pepper, then pour in the enchilada sauce and warm broth.
Spread level and make sure the rice is submerged.
Cover tightly with foil and bake 45 minutes.
Uncover, scatter the cheese over the top, and return uncovered for 10–15 minutes until melted and the chicken hits 165°F.
Rest 10 minutes so the rice drinks the last of the liquid, then divide into six.
swap: Swap the can of green chiles for half a diced jalapeño and use frozen corn instead of canned — about $1.50 off the batch. Store-brand Mexican cheese saves another $0.80.

ing: 2 tsp garlic powder · 1 tsp black pepper · 1½ tbsp smoked paprika
st: Season the chicken and pan-cook over medium-high, 5–7 minutes a side, until it reaches 165°F. Rest, then slice.
Boil the rotini to al dente and drain, saving a mug of the water.
Blend the cottage cheese, broth, parmesan, melted butter, garlic, salt and pepper until completely smooth.
Warm the sauce in the pan over low heat — do not let it boil or it splits.
Fold in the pasta, chicken, spinach and mozzarella, loosening with pasta water until it coats.
Divide into six containers.
swap: Parmesan is the one expensive line. Use half the parm plus a tablespoon of nutritional yeast, and skip the fat-free mozzarella — still creamy, about $1.60 cheaper.

st: Put the chicken in the slow cooker.
Whisk the orange juice, zest, soy sauce, honey, vinegar, garlic and ginger together and pour over.
Cook 3 hours on high or 8 hours on low.
Lift the chicken out, shred it, and whisk the potato starch into the sauce to thicken before returning the meat.
Cook the rice and steam the broccoli.
Build six bowls — rice, broccoli, chicken — and finish with sesame seeds.
swap: Frozen broccoli instead of fresh saves roughly $1.40/lb and holds up better in a container. Bottled orange juice is fine here — you only need the acid and the sugar.

ing: 1½ lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, bite-sized
2 tsp Italian seasoning · 1½ tsp garlic powder · 1 tsp onion powder · ¾ tsp smoked paprika · ¾ tsp salt · ½ tsp pepper
st: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Add the chicken, rice, onion, pepper, tomatoes, spinach and garlic to a baking dish.
Season, pour in the broth, and stir until the rice is submerged.
Cover tightly with foil and bake 45 minutes.
Uncover, add the parmesan, and bake another 15 minutes.
Finish with parsley and divide into six.
swap: Cherry tomatoes are $2.25 of this. A drained can of diced tomatoes costs a third and disappears into the rice anyway.

ing: 2½ lb boneless skinless chicken breast, diced
Cajun blend: 2 tsp smoked paprika · 2 tsp garlic powder · 1½ tsp onion powder · 1 tsp oregano · 1 tsp thyme · 1 tsp black pepper · ½–1 tsp cayenne · 1 tsp salt
st: Mix the Cajun seasoning and season the diced chicken with about two thirds of it.
Brown the chicken in oil over medium-high for 3–4 minutes — it does not need to cook through yet.
Add the onion and peppers for 2–3 minutes, then the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the uncooked pasta, broth and the rest of the seasoning. Bring to a gentle boil.
Cover, drop to medium-low and cook 10–13 minutes, stirring every few minutes so the pasta doesn't catch.
Off the heat, stir in the cream cheese and parmesan until it turns into a thick sauce.
Let it sit 2–3 minutes to thicken, then divide into six.
swap: Store-brand cream cheese saves $1.20, and building the Cajun blend from spice jars you already own beats buying a pre-mixed one.

ing: 1 tbsp Italian seasoning · 1 tsp garlic powder · 1 tsp onion powder · 1 tsp salt · ½ tsp pepper · ½ tsp red pepper flakes
st: Put the chicken in the slow cooker and season it.
Add the onion, garlic, crushed tomatoes, tomato sauce and paste. Sit the cream cheese on top.
Cook 3 hours on high or 5–6 on low, until the chicken pulls apart at 165°F.
Cook the pasta separately.
Shred the chicken and stir everything until the cream cheese disappears into the sauce.
Stir through the parmesan and mozzarella until melted, fold in the pasta, and finish with parsley.
swap: Store-brand cream cheese and mozzarella cut about $2.50. Crushed tomatoes go on sale under $1.20 regularly — buy two when they do.

ing: 2 tsp salt · 1 tsp pepper · 2 tsp garlic powder · 2 tsp onion powder · 2 tsp chili powder · 1 tsp cumin · juice of 1 lime
1½ cups jasmine rice, dry, cooked in 2¼ cups water
1 tbsp olive oil · 1 tsp garlic powder · 1 tsp salt · ½ tsp pepper
Sauce: 1 cup nonfat Greek yogurt · 2 cups cilantro · 2 limes · 1 tbsp minced garlic · 1 jalapeño · ½ tsp salt · 3 tbsp water
st: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Season the chicken and roast 25 minutes.
Toss the chopped vegetables in oil and seasoning and roast 25–30 minutes on a second tray.
Cook the rice.
Blend everything for the sauce, adding water until it pours.
Build six bowls and spoon the sauce over just before eating.
swap: The zucchini and two bell peppers are $5 of this batch. A bag of frozen pepper-and-onion mix plus one fresh zucchini does the same job for about $2.50.

ing: ½ tbsp cumin · ½ tbsp onion powder · 1 tsp allspice · 2 tsp turmeric · 1 tsp salt · 1 tsp pepper · ½ tbsp olive oil · ½ tbsp minced garlic · juice of ½ lemon · 2 tsp chicken bouillon
Rice: 1 tbsp butter · ½ yellow onion, chopped · 1 tbsp turmeric · 2 tsp garlic powder · 1 tsp pepper · 1 cup jasmine rice · 2 cups water
Salad: ½ red onion sliced · ½ cucumber · 24 cherry tomatoes · salt · pepper · juice of ½ lemon
Sauce: ½ cup nonfat Greek yogurt · ½ tbsp minced garlic · 1 tbsp parsley · 1 tsp salt · 1 tsp pepper · juice of ½ lemon · ½ tbsp olive oil
st: Marinate the thighs in the spice mix — an hour is good, overnight is better.
Soften the onion in butter, stir in the turmeric, garlic powder and pepper, add the rice and water, then simmer covered on low for 15–20 minutes.
Cook the chicken in a medium-high pan, 5 minutes a side, to 165°F. Rest, then slice.
Toss the salad ingredients together and whisk the sauce.
Build four bowls: rice, chicken, salad, sauce.
swap: Thighs are already the cheap cut, so the saving is in the salad: one diced whole tomato instead of 24 cherry tomatoes saves about $2.

ing: 2 tsp oregano · 1 tsp garlic powder · 2 tbsp smoked paprika · 1 tsp salt · ½ tsp pepper
Dressing: 240g nonfat Greek yogurt · 60g red wine vinegar · juice of 1 lemon · 2 tbsp olive oil · 15g Dijon · 2 tsp minced garlic · 2 tsp oregano · ½ tsp salt · ½ tsp pepper
st: Season and cook the chicken, then chill and dice it.
Cook the pasta, rinse it cold, and drain well.
Whisk the dressing, thinning with water until it pours.
Toss everything together — or keep the dressing separate and add it each morning, which keeps it crisp all week.
Divide into six.
swap: Artichoke hearts and Kalamata olives are $5 of this batch. Drop both and double the cucumber and tomato — still unmistakably Greek, and it falls to about $2.35 a meal.

ing: 2 tsp salt · 2 tsp garlic powder · 2 tsp onion powder · 2 tbsp smoked paprika · 1 tsp pepper
8 slices turkey or beef bacon — the post uses pork bacon
Sauce: 1 cup nonfat Greek yogurt · 2 tbsp ranch seasoning · 1 tsp dried parsley · water to thin
st: Air fry the seasoned chicken at 380°F for 18 minutes, flipping halfway.
Chop the bacon before cooking it in a pan to the crispness you want. Turkey bacon has less fat to render, so give it a little oil and pull it as soon as it browns.
Cook the penne and cool it.
Whisk the ranch sauce and thin it with water.
Toss everything with halved tomatoes and diced avocado.
Add the avocado the morning you eat it if you want it green.
swap: Bacon and avocado are $8.50 of this as the post writes it, with pork bacon. Turkey bacon roughly halves the bacon part, and an extra half cup of Greek yogurt replaces the avocado with protein instead of fat.

ing: 1 red bell pepper, diced · 1 large yellow onion, diced · 1 jalapeño, diced
Basil · green onions · roasted peanuts · furikake
Beef seasoning: 1½ tsp black pepper · 1½ tsp garlic powder · 1 tsp onion powder · 1 tsp smoked paprika
Sauce: 5 tbsp low-sodium soy · 2 tbsp oyster sauce · 2 tbsp sweet chilli · 1 tbsp honey · 1 tbsp rice vinegar · 2 tsp fish sauce · 5 cloves garlic minced · 2 tsp sriracha · ¼ cup water
st: Cook the rice and set it aside.
Whisk all the sauce ingredients together.
Cook the seasoned beef in a hot skillet, then lift it out.
In the same pan, char the pepper, onion and jalapeño for 5–7 minutes, letting them sit still between tosses.
Return the beef, pour in the sauce, and cook 2–3 minutes until it reduces and coats.
Wilt the basil through, then divide over rice and top with peanuts and furikake.
swap: Ground chicken or turkey instead of beef saves about $8 on the batch. Skip the oyster and fish sauce and add another splash of soy plus a pinch of sugar.

ing: 2 tsp garlic powder · 2 tsp onion powder · 1 tbsp smoked paprika · 1 tsp salt · 1 tsp pepper
2 bags (48 oz) baby Dutch yellow potatoes — russets cut this by $2.45
7 slices turkey or beef bacon — the post uses pork bacon
st: Air fry the potatoes at 400°F for 28 minutes, shaking halfway.
Brown the seasoned beef.
Cook and chop the bacon.
Build six containers: potatoes, beef, cheese, then yogurt, onions and jalapeños added when you eat.
Swap the beef for diced chicken breast to drop this from $5.13 to about $2.90 a serving.
swap: Two swaps turn this from the priciest recipe here into one of the cheapest: russets instead of baby Dutch potatoes (−$2.45) and diced chicken breast instead of ground beef (−$9.60). That is $5.13 down to about $2.40 a serving.

ing: 1 tsp garlic powder · ½ tsp Italian seasoning · ½ tsp salt · ¼ tsp black pepper
st: Blend the cottage cheese, eggs, parmesan, milk, cornstarch and seasonings until completely smooth.
Warm the sauce in a pan over medium-low for 3–5 minutes, stirring often. Do not let it boil.
Toss with hot pasta, loosening with a splash of pasta water.
The whole batch of sauce is around 560 calories and 60g of protein — add grilled chicken or roasted vegetables to make it a full meal.
swap: Already the cheapest thing in the book. If you want it cheaper still, more milk and less parmesan keeps the texture.

ing: 2 tbsp Italian mixed herbs · 1 tbsp chilli powder · 2 tbsp paprika
st: Air fry the sweet potatoes at 190°C / 375°F for 40–45 minutes, turning halfway. In an oven, 200°C / 400°F for 50–60 minutes.
Brown the mince with the onion, garlic and spices, then stir in the tomato paste and spinach.
Split the potatoes, fluff the insides, and fill.
Top with mozzarella and return until it melts.
Ground chicken here drops the cost by about $2.80 a boat.
swap: Ground chicken instead of beef saves about $2.80 a boat. Regular mozzarella is cheaper than the 'light' version and melts better.

ing: ½ tbsp each garlic powder, onion powder, ground cumin, paprika
Lemon juice or garlic aioli to dress
st: Toss the dried chickpeas with the spices and oil and bake at 180°C / 355°F for 15 minutes, turning once, until lightly golden.
Cook the couscous and let it cool.
Toss everything together.
Dress with a squeeze of lemon, or aioli if you want it richer.
swap: Dried chickpeas soaked overnight cost about a third of canned. Frozen corn instead of fresh, and any grain you have instead of couscous.

ing: Cracked black pepper · salt to taste
st: Slice the peaches and pile everything into a bowl.
Dress with good olive oil and balsamic glaze.
Crack pepper over and serve immediately — this one does not keep.
swap: Candied pecans are the splurge. Toast plain walnuts in a dry pan with a teaspoon of honey — a quarter of the price and better.

ing: Biscoff chia pot: 20g chia seeds (replacing the 30g of oats) · 50g nonfat Greek yogurt · 30g protein powder · a splash of milk · 1 Lotus Biscoff cookie
Protein pancake bowls: 1 medium egg · 30g all-purpose flour · 30g protein powder · 100ml water · banana · chocolate chips
Beef, rice and beans: 85g basmati rice · 190g green beans · 150g low-fat ground beef
st: Chia pot: stir together with a splash of milk and leave in the fridge overnight — chia needs more liquid than the oats did.
Pancake bowls: mix the batter, pour into a dish, and air fry 10 minutes at 180°C / 355°F. Top with banana and chocolate chips.
Beef bowl: cook the rice, steam the green beans, brown the beef, and box all three together.
Three components, one session — this is the leanest full-day prep in the book.
swap: Plain whey instead of a branded protein powder, and own-brand caramelised biscuits instead of Lotus. Frozen green beans instead of fresh.

ing: 5 slices turkey bacon, cooked and diced
½ tsp salt · ¼ tsp black pepper · ½ tsp garlic powder · ¼ tsp onion powder
st: Heat the oven to 300°F.
Cook the turkey bacon until crisp and dice it small.
Blend the eggs, whites, cottage cheese and seasonings until completely smooth.
Stir in the mozzarella and bacon.
Fill a greased or silicone-lined 12-cup muffin tin about ¾ full.
Bake 35 minutes, until the centres are just set.
Cool 5–10 minutes before lifting them out. Three bites is a serving; they keep 5 days cold or 2 months frozen, and reheat in 30–45 seconds.
swap: Skip the turkey bacon entirely — the cottage cheese is doing the work — and use store-brand mozzarella. Drops to about $1.05 a serving.

ing: 2 cups frozen bell pepper and onion mix
Salt, pepper and garlic to taste
st: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Whisk the eggs, liquid eggs and cottage cheese together and season.
Fold in the hash browns, zucchini, pepper-and-onion mix, bacon and cheese.
Pour into a large baking dish and bake 40–45 minutes. Check at 40 — a deeper dish will want longer.
Scatter green onions over and cut into six.
swap: Frozen diced potatoes instead of branded hash browns saves about $1.20, and dropping the turkey bacon still leaves you above 40g of protein.

ing: ¼ cup all-purpose flour — replaces the ⅓ cup of oats
st: Blend everything until smooth.
Let the batter rest 5 minutes — this is what stops them being rubbery.
Pour onto a lightly greased skillet over medium-low.
Cook 2–3 minutes a side, flipping once bubbles form and the edges set.
Makes four medium pancakes.
The creator blended ⅓ cup of oats into flour for these. Plain all-purpose flour does the same job — the macros shown are my recalculation for that swap.
swap: Leave out the scoop of whey and use 150g of Greek yogurt plus one extra egg — saves $0.81 and costs you about 8g of protein.

ing: 2 tbsp chia seeds — replaces the ½ cup of oats
¾ cup nonfat plain Greek yogurt
A splash of milk to loosen
st: Stir the chia, protein powder, yogurt, jello powder and a splash of milk together.
Fold in the blueberries.
Leave overnight — the chia needs the full night to gel, more than oats did.
Built with oats the creator had this at 449 cal and 54g protein. The chia version shown here is my recalculation: slightly fewer carbs, a bit more fat, protein essentially unchanged.
swap: Without the whey this is $1.68 and still carries 30g of protein from the yogurt alone. Frozen blueberries cost half what fresh do.

ing: 80g quinoa flakes — a straight one-for-one swap for the 80g of oats
st: Stir everything together in a jar and refrigerate overnight.

Quinoa flakes behave almost exactly like rolled oats here — same soak, same texture, near-identical macros. They cost more, so the cheap alternative is 200g of leftover cooked rice, which turns this into a protein rice pudding.
This is a big breakfast at around 800 calories. Drop the peanut butter and chia to bring it near 550 without touching the protein.
Whole milk instead of almond takes it higher if you are trying to gain.
swap: Regular milk instead of almond is cheaper and adds protein. Store-brand peanut butter, and buy bananas when they are spotted and cheap, then freeze them.

st: Whisk the eggs, whites, cinnamon, stevia and vanilla into a custard.
Soak each slice and griddle until golden on both sides.
Drizzle with the melted dark chocolate.
Macros are per slice — this makes twenty, so it is a fortnight of breakfasts. Freeze flat with parchment between the slices.
swap: Store-brand thick white bread instead of two brioche loaves cuts about $6 off the batch. You lose richness, not protein.

ing: A generous handful of grated parmesan
st: Lay the tomatoes cut-side down in an oiled pan, salt them, cover, and cook over medium-low for 5–8 minutes until the skins loosen.
Peel the skins off with tongs, then crush the tomatoes in the pan.
Add the chopped garlic for 30–60 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste, confit and another pinch of salt to build a chunky base.
Stir a good amount of parmesan through until creamy.
Make three wells, crack the eggs in, cover, and cook 5 minutes for set whites and jammy yolks.
Finish with more parmesan and parsley.
swap: Out of season, a can of whole peeled tomatoes is cheaper and genuinely better than pale winter fresh ones. Skip the garlic confit.

ing: Each marinade is for about 1.5 lb of chicken
Greek lemon yogurt: 1 cup Greek yogurt · ¼ cup olive oil · 4 garlic cloves minced · 1 tbsp oregano · juice of ½ lemon · ¼ cup parsley
Honey garlic: 2 tbsp olive oil · 2 tbsp soy sauce · ¼ cup honey · 2 garlic cloves minced · ⅓ cup sliced green onions
Spicy mango: 1 mango puréed · 3 tbsp olive oil · juice of ½ lime · 2 garlic cloves minced · sliced jalapeños
Cilantro lime: 2 tbsp olive oil · juice of 1 lime · 2 tbsp honey · ½ cup fresh cilantro · 2 garlic cloves minced
Chicken asado: juice of ½ orange · 2 tbsp avocado oil · juice of ½ lime · 1 tsp each chilli powder, cumin, oregano, paprika, garlic powder
st: Buy one big tray of chicken breast and split it five ways.
Mix each marinade in its own freezer bag and add the chicken.
Freeze them flat. They marinate as they thaw, so a bag moved to the fridge in the morning is ready that evening.
This is the single highest-leverage habit in the book — it turns the cheapest protein into five different meals with no extra cooking time.
swap: The whole saving here is buying the single biggest chicken tray you can carry and splitting it five ways. Use whatever citrus is cheapest that week.

st: Stir everything until smooth.
Spread into a lined tray and add your toppings.
Freeze at least 90 minutes, then break into bars.
Four bars is a serving at 34g of protein and one gram of fat.
swap: Without the scoop of whey these are $0.42 a serving and still 25g of protein from the yogurt.

ing: ¾ cup all-purpose flour — replaces the 1 cup of blended oats
st: Heat the oven to 370°F.
Mash the banana and mix everything together.
Bake 15–20 minutes, until a toothpick comes out mostly clean.
Cool 10–15 minutes before slicing, or they fall apart.
swap: Peanut butter powder is the pricey line. Two tablespoons of ordinary peanut butter works and costs less per batch.

ing: 1 sweet potato, steamed or baked, skin off
st: Blend everything except the chocolate chips.
Pour into a greased 5×7 baking dish and scatter the chips over.
Bake at 350°F for 30 minutes.
Cool completely before cutting.
swap: Regular chocolate chips instead of sugar-free saves about $0.75, and any cheap sweetener stands in for the honey.

st: Brown the beef and season it.
Build the tortilla and fold.
Double everything and it becomes a 60g-protein meal — this is the fastest thing in the book after a session.
swap: 96/4 is a premium grind. 93/7 is about a dollar less a pound and you will not notice it inside a wrap.

ing: ¼ tsp turmeric powder, or a piece of fresh turmeric
st: Put the 1.5 litres of coconut water in the blender.
Chop the lime, lemon, grapefruit and green apple and add them.
Blend until completely smooth.
Add the turmeric and blend again, then stir in the honey.
Strain through a nut-milk bag into small bottles.
Keeps 10–12 days in the fridge; freeze whatever you will not drink in that window.
swap: Coconut water is most of the cost here. Plain water plus one extra lime does the same job for roughly $4 less a batch.

ing: 2 thick slices sourdough or brioche — or any thick store-brand bread
1½–2 tbsp pumpkin spice peanut butter — or plain peanut butter plus ¼ tsp pumpkin pie spice
½ tsp butter or cooking spray
Toppings: ¼ cup Greek yogurt · pumpkin spice · crushed pecans · a small drizzle of maple syrup
st: Spread the peanut butter on one slice, lay the banana over it, and close the sandwich.
Whisk the egg, milk, vanilla, cinnamon and salt into a custard.
Soak the whole sandwich in it, both sides, letting it drink for a few seconds.
Griddle in butter over medium until golden and crisp on both sides, 3–4 minutes a side.
Top with Greek yogurt, a dusting of pumpkin spice, pecans and the maple drizzle.
The creator didn't publish macros for this one. Built as written with Greek yogurt on top it lands around 30g of protein.
swap: This is the one you flagged, and you were right — the recipe is good, the shopping list is not. Plain peanut butter with ¼ tsp of pumpkin pie spice stirred in replaces the $8 specialty jar. Thick store-brand bread instead of brioche, walnuts instead of pecans, and the Greek yogurt on top you already have in the fridge. Built that way it comes to about $1.58 a serving instead of roughly $3.40.

ing: 2 tsp Italian seasoning · 1½ tsp garlic powder · 1 tsp salt · 1 tsp black pepper · ½ tsp red pepper flakes
st: Heat the oven to 400°F. Put the tomatoes, zucchini, shallot and garlic cloves in a 9×13 dish with the Boursin in the middle.
Drizzle with oil, season, and bake 30–35 minutes.
Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces, season with the garlic powder, salt and pepper, and cook in a skillet over medium-high for 7–10 minutes until browned through.
Cook the rigatoni to just al dente.
Burst the roasted tomatoes and mash the garlic into the Boursin, leaving the zucchini mostly intact.
Fold in the pasta, chicken, basil and the juice of the lemon until everything is coated.
swap: Boursin is $4.50 for 5.3 oz. Blend ¾ cup of cottage cheese with two cloves of garlic, a teaspoon of Italian seasoning and a pinch of salt — same creamy sauce, roughly triple the protein, about $3.50 cheaper. That takes this from $3.70 to about $3.12 a serving.

st: Whisk everything together until completely smooth.
Pour into a lined tin.
Bake at 200°C / 390°F for around 45 minutes.
Cool before slicing into four.
The whole thing is 661 calories and 66g of protein — the macros shown are per slice.
swap: Plain Greek yogurt plus a scoop of vanilla whey costs less than branded protein yoghurt and gets you the same set.

st: Wash and roughly chop the ginger and turmeric.
Blend them with a little water until they turn into a paste.
Bring the half gallon of water to a boil in a large pot, then take it off the heat.
Stir the paste into the hot water along with the cayenne and black pepper.
Cover and leave it to steep at least 2 hours.
Strain and refrigerate.
Serve 8–12 oz hot or cold with a teaspoon of raw honey and half a squeezed lemon or orange.
The black pepper is not optional — it is what makes the turmeric absorbable.
swap: Ground turmeric instead of fresh works and costs a fraction. Buy ginger from an Asian or halal market — it is routinely half the supermarket price.

ing: 1½ cups freshly squeezed lemon juice (6–8 large lemons)
st: Zest three lemons into a bowl, avoiding the white pith.
Add the sugar and rub the two together with your fingers for 2–3 minutes, until fragrant — the sugar's grit pulls the aromatic oils out of the zest. This is the whole trick.
Roll the lemons under your palm to loosen them, then juice 6–8 of them into the bowl. You want about 1½ cups.
Store the base in a container in the fridge.
To serve, mix 1 part base to 4–6 parts water, to taste, over ice.
swap: Bagged lemons beat loose ones by a wide margin. Do not substitute bottled juice — the zest-and-sugar rub is the entire point of this recipe.

ing: 1 lungo (a large espresso, has to be hot)
A piece of butter, roughly a tsp
st: Pull the espresso hot.
Add the butter, maple syrup and salt, and froth until the butter has completely dissolved.
Fill a glass with ice and pour in the milk.
Pour the espresso mixture over the top.
A little more salt on top if you like it.
swap: Real maple syrup is the cost. Half maple, half brown sugar dissolved in a splash of hot water gets most of the way there.

ing: 1 pack chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 tsp garlic powder · 1 tsp chilli powder · 1 tsp paprika · 1 tsp cumin · salt
Tajín (optional — the creator says it's excellent without)
st: Cube the chicken and coat it in all the spices. Set aside, and start your rice now so it's ready at the end.
Make the corn topping: blend the cottage cheese smooth, then stir it through the drained corn with the jalapeño, cilantro, lime juice and salt. Hold back some cilantro to finish.
Cook the chicken over medium heat in a cast iron pan.
Build the bowls — rice, chicken, corn topping, sliced avocado, the reserved cilantro.
The creator published no macros. On my own count with a 1.5 lb pack of breast this is roughly 42g of protein a bowl.
swap: The avocado is a third of the cost and goes brown in a container anyway — leave it out of the batch and slice one fresh onto whichever bowl you are eating. Frozen corn instead of canned saves another $0.40.

ing: Pinch each of paprika, cumin, onion powder, garlic powder, Cajun seasoning and salt
1 tbsp Cajun seasoning · 1 tbsp taco seasoning · cumin · salt
Sauce: a little cilantro or parsley · 1 clove garlic, minced · 1 tsp mayonnaise · 1 cup Greek yogurt · zest and juice of 1 lemon
st: Season the chicken breasts with the spice mix.
Cook in a hot pan or air fryer with a little oil until golden on each side. When you flip to the second side, cover it — that is what gets the inside done without drying the outside.
Cook the rice, then toss it with the peppers, corn, kidney beans, Cajun and taco seasoning, cumin and salt.
Blend everything for the sauce in a food processor until smooth.
Slice the chicken over the rice and spoon the sauce across.
Translated from the creator's Arabic caption. No macros were published.
swap: Two bell peppers are $3 of this. One pepper plus a bag of frozen pepper strips does the same for about a third. Skip the mayonnaise — the yogurt sauce does not need it.

ing: A blade or chuck cut of beef, about 3 lb
Garlic · salt · pepper · rosemary · thyme · butter — pounded together in a mortar
Salt, pepper and smoked paprika to season the meat
More butter and whatever sauce you like, to finish
st: Pound the garlic, salt, pepper, rosemary, thyme and butter into a paste in a mortar.
Season the beef all over with salt, pepper and smoked paprika.
Rub the butter paste into the meat thoroughly.
Sit it in a tray with beef stock.
Roast low and slow for 3–4 hours.
Brush with butter and sauce, then finish for half an hour under the grill.

One caution on the original: the caption gives the oven at 60°C, which is a sous-vide temperature, not an oven one — a large roast held there for hours sits in the bacterial danger zone. Cook it at 150°C / 300°F for the same 3–4 hours instead. Same result, and safe.
swap: Blade and chuck are already the cheap end of beef, which is the whole point of a long roast. Buy the biggest piece on offer and eat it across three days.

ing: 300g crisp rice cereal plus 150g crushed roasted peanuts — replacing the 450g of oats in the original
1 cup (250ml) coconut cream or any thick cream
st: Whisk the coconut cream in a bowl until smooth.
Stir in the honey and mix well.
Add the peanut butter and work it through with a spoon.
Add the crisp rice and crushed peanuts and mix thoroughly — you will need your hands for this.
Press the mixture flat into a tray.
Chill overnight, or at least two hours, then cut into 12–16 bars.
The original is an oat bar; the crisp rice and peanut mix keeps the same bind and crunch without them. Nothing else changes.
swap: Priced with Great Value crisp rice at $3.74 for 24 oz and own-brand peanuts at $2.58 a pound, these land at about $0.56 a bar. Evaporated milk stands in for coconut cream at half the price.

ing: 1 cup creamy almond butter — peanut butter works and costs a fifth as much
st: Heat the oven to 350°F and line an 8-inch square pan with parchment.
Stir the mashed sweet potato, nut butter, cocoa powder and maple syrup together until blended.
Fold in the chocolate chips.
Spread evenly in the pan.
Bake 18–21 minutes, until a toothpick comes out with moist crumbs.
Cool in the pan before slicing into sixteen.
The caption only listed the five ingredients, so I pulled the quantities and the creator's macros from her recipe page.
swap: Almond butter is $7 a jar. Plain peanut butter costs about a fifth of that and is indistinguishable under this much cocoa — that swap alone takes these from roughly $1.10 to $0.39 a brownie.

st: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for about a minute, until you can smell them.
Grind the black seed well, then stir the toasted sesame through it.
Mix into the honey until it comes together as a firm paste.
Spread it on a sandwich, or take a spoonful on its own.
Translated from the creator's Arabic caption.
swap: Buy the nigella and sesame from a halal or Middle Eastern grocer rather than the supermarket spice aisle — routinely a quarter of the price for ten times the quantity.

st: Peel and roughly chop everything.
Blend with enough water to get it moving, then strain if you want it thin.
Serve over ice.

Read this one with an asterisk: the post had no caption at all, so the ingredients here come from the comment thread under it, where the creator and viewers name beet, carrot, pineapple and ginger. The quantities are mine, not hers.
Several commenters made the fair point that eating the beets, carrots and pineapple whole gets you the fibre that juicing throws away.
swap: Beets are cheapest loose and unwashed. Frozen pineapple chunks cost less than a fresh one and you are blending it anyway.

ing: 2 lb boneless skinless chicken breast, diced
1 (14 oz) can artichoke hearts, drained and chopped
1½ tsp garlic powder · 1 tsp onion powder · 1 tsp oregano · 1 tsp Italian seasoning · ½ tsp red pepper flakes · ½ tsp black pepper · ½ tsp salt
st: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Put the dry orzo, raw diced chicken, artichokes, onion, garlic, olive oil, seasonings and the 2 cups of broth straight into a deep 9×13 dish. Mix so the orzo is mostly submerged.
Cover tightly with foil and bake 40 minutes, until the orzo is tender and the chicken reaches 165°F.
While it's still hot, stir in the cream cheese, parmesan and lemon juice until smooth.
Fold the spinach through until wilted.
Divide into six containers.
Note the creator corrected these macros after posting — he'd left the parmesan out of the original calculation. The numbers here are his corrected ones.
swap: The can of artichoke hearts is $3.63 and the reduced-fat cream cheese $2.50. Store-brand cream cheese saves a dollar; halving the artichokes and adding more spinach saves nearly two more and barely changes the dish.

ing: 1½ tsp oregano · 1 tsp smoked paprika · ½ tsp onion powder · ½ tsp red pepper flakes · ½ tsp salt
st: Heat the oven to 400°F. Sit the Boursin in the centre of a 9×13 dish and add the salmon, tomatoes, shallot and garlic around it. Drizzle with oil and season.
Bake 25–30 minutes, until the salmon hits 145°F and the tomatoes collapse.
Cook the rotini to al dente while it bakes, then drain.
Squeeze the lemon over everything. Burst the tomatoes, flake the salmon, and stir it all through the Boursin until creamy.
Add the pasta and spinach and toss until the spinach wilts.
Divide into six.
Straight-up warning: built exactly as written this is the most expensive thing in the book at $6.45 a serving — sockeye runs $15.98/lb. The cheaper version is below and it is a big drop.
swap: Three swaps take this from $6.45 to about $2.63 a serving — the biggest single saving in the book. Great Value wild-caught pink salmon is $12.47 for 32 oz against sockeye's $15.98 a pound, so the fish alone drops from $23.97 to $9.36. Blend ¾ cup of cottage cheese with garlic and Italian herbs instead of the Boursin. And a drained can of diced tomatoes replaces two pints of cherry tomatoes for about a fifth of the price.

ing: Zaziki: 500g skyr or thick yogurt · ½ cucumber, grated · ½ bunch parsley · ½ bunch dill · juice of 1 lemon · 2 tsp garlic powder · 1 tsp thyme · 1 tbsp olive oil · salt and pepper
Potatoes: 500g baby potatoes · 2 tsp paprika · 1 tsp rosemary · 1 tsp salt · a few sprays of oil
Tofu döner: 400g smoked tofu · a little oil · 4 tbsp soy sauce · 3 tbsp maple syrup · 2 tbsp smoked paprika · 1 tbsp onion granules · 1 tbsp garlic powder · splash of water if needed
To finish: 150g red cabbage · 150g cherry tomatoes · 150g cucumber (with parsley, salt and pepper) · 150g lettuce
st: Halve the potatoes, toss with the spices and oil, lay cut-side down on a tray, smash each one flat, and bake 25–30 minutes at 180°C fan / 350°F.
Mix everything for the zaziki and set it aside.
Grate the smoked tofu, fry it in a little oil, drop the heat and stir in the soy, maple syrup and spices. Add a splash of water if it goes dry.
Chop the tomato and cucumber and toss with parsley, salt and pepper.
Build it all in a bowl and eat it straight away — the potatoes lose their crunch if this sits.

The Instagram caption sends you to a DM for the recipe. The quantities here come from the same creator's own post of this dish on TikTok, where the full method is public, and the macros match the ones on the Instagram post exactly: 1503 cal and 128g protein for the whole thing, which is what the per-serving figures here are divided from.
swap: This is produce-heavy, which is where the money goes. Plain Greek yogurt instead of a vegan skyr saves about $2.20 on its own. Buy the cabbage as a wedge rather than a bag, use whatever lettuce is on offer, and swap the fresh dill for dried.

st: Blend the ginger and turmeric with 1 cup of water, then tip into a pot with another 3¼ cups of water. Grating them by hand into 1 litre of water works too.
Add the freshly ground black pepper and the cayenne.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Cool and store in glass jars in the fridge.
Add the lemon juice, olive oil and honey cold, just before drinking, not to the hot pot.

Two things the creator explains that are worth keeping: the simmer is the point — it converts the ginger's gingerols into shogaols and makes the batch keep longer — and the olive oil is there because curcumin needs a fat to be absorbed at all. The health claims in the post are his; the technique is sound either way.
This is the third ginger drink in your saves. The other two are quicker; this one keeps the longest.
swap: Turmeric root is the expensive line at five or six thumbs. Ground turmeric works — about 2 tbsp — and costs a fraction. Buy ginger from a halal or Asian grocer, routinely half the supermarket price.

ing: 2 cups dry jasmine rice plus 3 cups water
10g salt, pepper and garlic seasoning — the post uses Kinder's The Blend
st: Cook the rice: 2 cups of rice to 3 cups of water in a rice cooker.
Brown all 3 lb of beef in a large pan with the seasoning. When it's about halfway cooked, pour in the 16 oz of egg whites and let them cook through with the beef.
Chop the bacon and fry it over medium heat until browned and crisp.
Off the heat, mix the rice, bacon and mozzarella into the beef until the cheese melts.
Divide into 7 containers. Refrigerate within 2 hours, eat the fridge ones within 3–4 days, and freeze the rest.
Reheat 1½ minutes from the fridge. From frozen, add a splash of water, cover with a paper towel and heat 5 minutes.

The creator pours sugar-free syrup over each bowl. That's sweeteners, which you said you're avoiding — a teaspoon of real maple syrup does the same sweet-and-savoury job for about 17 calories. His macros leave the syrup out either way.
The post doesn't give the mozzarella bag size. An 8 oz bag is what makes the numbers land near his 631 calories and 65g of protein.
swap: 96/4 grass-fed at Walmart is $7.88 a pound — oddly, a few cents less than its conventional 93/7 — so the saving is in the protein swap. Shady Brook 93/7 ground turkey at $5.56/lb and Butterball turkey bacon instead of beef bacon take it from $5.33 to about $3.71 a bowl with nearly the same protein.

ing: Chilli flakes, oregano, salt and pepper
A few sprays of olive oil
st: Heat the oven to 200°C / 400°F.
Put the cherry tomatoes and courgette in a large oven-safe pan, sit the Boursin in the middle, spray with oil and season with chilli flakes, oregano, salt and pepper.
Roast until the tomatoes burst and the Boursin softens.
Meanwhile, cook the orzo in salted water and drain — the creator confirmed in the comments that he cooks it first.
Stir the tomatoes, courgette and Boursin into a sauce, then fold in the orzo, chicken and torn basil.
Top with the parmesan and go back in the oven until golden. He puts the total oven time at 20–30 minutes at 200°C.
Divide into four.
Warren ran out of Boursin the second time he made it and used Philadelphia Lightest instead — he says it was just as good. The recipe itself is from @adamhoadcoaching.
swap: The 800g of cherry tomatoes is $8.38 of this. Two cans of diced tomatoes do the same job for $1.92. Blend ¾ cup of cottage cheese with garlic and Italian herbs instead of the Boursin, and use dried basil. That takes it from $5.50 to about $2.45 a serving.

st: Heat the oven to 180°C / 350°F.
Put the salmon, spinach, cream cheese and cherry tomatoes in a baking dish. Drizzle with olive oil and season.
Bake 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta according to the packet.
Flake the salmon and stir everything through the pasta until it turns creamy. Parmesan on top if you like.

The serving count and macros are mine — the post gives neither. With 350g of salmon this makes three normal plates at about 34g of protein each. As two plates it is nearly 1,000 calories each, mostly from the cream cheese.
Costed with fresh Atlantic salmon at $10.64/lb, which is what the fillet in the video looks like.
swap: Great Value wild-caught pink salmon at $6.24/lb instead of fresh Atlantic, and 150g of cottage cheese instead of the cream cheese. It drops from $3.87 to about $2.61 a serving, and the cottage cheese takes out most of the fat.

ing: 1 tsp paprika and a little olive oil, for the corn
Dressing: 4 tbsp plain yogurt · juice of ½ lemon · 3–4 tbsp olive oil · 1 garlic clove or 1 tsp granulated garlic · a handful of grated parmesan or crumbled feta · 1 tsp honey · salt and pepper
st: Rinse the corn and drain it very well, then toss it with the paprika and a little olive oil.
Air-fry at 200°C / 390°F for 15 minutes, shaking the basket halfway, until crisp.
Chop the lettuce, cucumbers, tomatoes, onion and parsley small.
Whisk the dressing together and toss it through the salad.
Add the crunchy corn last, just before eating, so it stays crisp. For meal prep, keep the corn and dressing in separate containers.
The creator's tip: if you leave the parmesan out of the dressing, cubes of firm white cheese in the salad work well.

This is a side, at about 7g of protein a serving. Put it next to one of the chicken or salmon recipes, or stir in a drained can of chickpeas to make it a meal. The post gives no macros, so these are my estimates, and they are mostly olive oil — use 2 tbsp in the dressing to cut about 60 calories a serving.
swap: Cherry tomatoes are the biggest line at about $2.70. Two Roma tomatoes cost $0.44 and do the same job. Leave the parmesan out and use the feta the creator suggests, or nothing. That comes to about $1.55 a serving.

ing: 6 cl (¼ cup) melted butter — the post allows neutral oil or butter; butter keeps it free of seed oil
st: Heat the oven to 180°C / 350°F and line a loaf tin.
Mash three bananas and keep the fourth to halve lengthwise for the top.
Whisk the eggs with both sugars, then add the melted butter, yogurt and vanilla.
Fold in the flour and baking powder, then the chocolate and nuts.
Pour into the tin and lay the banana halves on top.
Bake 30 minutes at 180°C — that's the creator's own answer in the comments. Check with a skewer; a deep loaf can need 10–15 minutes more.
Cool before cutting into 10 slices.
This one is a treat rather than a protein snack, at about 5g a slice. Swapping 30g of the flour for a scoop of vanilla whey roughly doubles that. Macros are my estimate; the post gives none.
swap: Already about $0.45 a slice. Walnuts are the priciest line at $1.10 — use peanuts or leave them out, and it's $0.34. One 3.5 oz bar of Great Value dark chocolate covers two loaves.
